title: Reflector
summary: A governed, auditable research system for keeping recursive AI-assisted engineering aligned with human intent from source through publication.
problem: Recursive AI workflows can move faster than people can inspect them, allowing code, research claims, metadata, and release artifacts to drift apart.
constraints: The work is public and draft-stage, so every claim must stay inspectable, publication builds must be repeatable, and the DOI-backed artifact must not be presented as peer-reviewed research.
decisions: Model human governance, synchronization checkpoints, explicit specifications, and deterministic publication as first-class system contracts instead of relying on prompt discipline alone.
implementation: A Python CLI, manuscript source, machine-readable publication metadata, specification contracts, audit archives, deterministic paper builds, and GitHub Pages publication workflows live in one layered repository.
validation: Task-driven doctor, test, and example checks sit beside CI for the paper build, Pages publication, metadata, and REUSE compliance.
outcome: A public, DOI-backed independent research artifact and reference implementation that can be inspected from its source and governance model through its published output.
role: System architecture, implementation, research workflow design, and public repository stewardship.
aiAssistance: AI-assisted implementation and drafting operate inside specifications, audit checkpoints, deterministic checks, and human review and release decisions.

title: Renderflow
summary: A Rust, specification-driven rendering engine that plans repeatable transformations from source documents to publication-ready outputs.
problem: Multi-format publishing often becomes a collection of fragile shell commands, duplicated intermediate work, and renderer-specific flags that are difficult to audit or reproduce.
constraints: One configuration must support multiple outputs, preserve a dry-run path, remain useful as both a CLI and an SDK, and keep external rendering tools behind clear boundaries.
decisions: Represent formats and transformations as a directed acyclic graph, select paths through explicit optimization modes, share intermediates, and execute independent conversion waves in parallel.
implementation: A Rust workspace separates the graph engine and SDK, CLI adapter, and plugin boundary, with YAML specifications, pluggable transforms, content-hash caching, and Pandoc, Tectonic, and FFmpeg integrations.
validation: The public repository exposes CI, tests, generated documentation, dry-run and doctor commands, release automation, and cross-platform artifact checks.
outcome: An inspectable rendering engine and reusable library with explicit build plans, multi-target output, and a documented release surface—without making adoption or production-scale claims.
role: System architecture, Rust implementation, developer-experience design, and release workflow stewardship.
aiAssistance: Optional AI transforms are isolated from the core planner; implementation assistance remains bounded by specifications, code review, tests, and owner-controlled releases.

title: Relay
summary: A versioned catalog of reusable GitHub Actions and workflows that turns proven repository automation into reviewable platform contracts.
problem: Copying CI implementation between repositories creates drift, obscures ownership, and makes security or release improvements difficult to propagate safely.
constraints: Consumer repositories must retain permissions and deployment ownership, production callers need immutable pins, and private collection data must never leak into public Pages artifacts.
decisions: Publish small versioned contracts, recommend full-commit SHA pins, preserve one Pages owner per repository, and make public-safe provenance an explicit publication gate.
implementation: Composite actions, reusable workflows, a machine-readable action catalog, a framework-free repository-intelligence builder, and a guarded release manifest define the reusable surface.
validation: Local validation covers action metadata, JSON contracts, Python unit tests and compilation; CI additionally checks Bash syntax, workflow structure, and release invariants.
outcome: A reusable automation layer with explicit provider, policy, consumer, and deployment boundaries—presented as a public engineering system without unsupported adoption metrics.
role: Platform architecture, workflow implementation, contract design, and release governance.
aiAssistance: AI-assisted implementation is kept inside bounded pull requests; permission, provenance, security, contract, and release decisions remain human-owned.

title: Optiflow
summary: A deliberately read-only Rust CLI for inventorying media, proving exact duplicates, and producing immutable review plans before any future mutation exists.
problem: Large personal media collections accumulate duplicates, but destructive cleanup is unsafe when identity, filesystem state, and reclaimable storage have not been proven first.
constraints: The tool must stay local-first, behave conservatively on removable storage, expose stable machine contracts, and guarantee that version 0.1.0 cannot delete, move, replace, or quarantine files.
decisions: Separate observation from action, narrow candidates by byte length before complete hashing, preserve immutable evidence artifacts, and require future apply-time revalidation and byte comparison.
implementation: A Rust CLI combines conservative scanning, optional ffprobe inspection, local SQLite state, BLAKE3 hashing, schema-versioned JSON envelopes, and deterministic duplicate-planning commands.
validation: Formatting, Clippy, tests, contract checks, and an end-to-end smoke test use synthetic paths—including spaces and Unicode—and verify both duplicate inputs remain unchanged.
outcome: Inspectable inventory, exact-duplicate evidence, reclaimable-storage estimates, and review plans are available without introducing a file-mutation path.
role: Safety model, system architecture, Rust implementation, CLI contracts, and validation design.
aiAssistance: AI-assisted implementation is constrained by the read-only product boundary, versioned schemas, explicit safety invariants, tests, and human release decisions.
